mainTopic: The meaning of מבעה, and how the lists of main damages from the משנה, רבי אושעיא (thirteen) and רבי חייא (twenty-four) fit together.
overview: This amud first finishes an earlier answer for רב: the משנה teaches that a person is responsible to guard his own body. Next, רב מרי suggests that מבעה means damage by water, and רב זביד suggests it means fire. The גמרא rejects both ideas using the grammar of a פסוק and the wording of the משנה. Then רבי אושעיא counts thirteen main categories of damage: four kinds of watchmen, five payments for injuring a person, and the four of our משנה. The גמרא explains why our משנה and רבי אושעיא list things differently. It does this by splitting 'person' into two kinds and by telling apart direct damage from damage that happens on its own. Finally, רבי חייא counts twenty-four categories, adding fines and theft. The גמרא explains that רבי אושעיא leaves out fines, and that רבי חייא separates money a person received in a permitted way from money he took in a forbidden way.

steps.title: Read the משנה as: a person must guard his own body
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes an earlier answer. Read the משנה as teaching that a person (אדם) is responsible for guarding his own body.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, teach it this way: a person is responsible for guarding his own body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes an earlier back-and-forth. It tells us how to read a line of the משנה according to רב's view that מבעה means a person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'here too' shows that the גמרא is using the same reading method it used just before. The line is read as teaching that a person himself carries the duty of watching over his own body. This keeps רב's explanation of מבעה working with the words of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too; the same applies in this case
Teach it (read the text) this way
The guarding of his own body

phrases.english: Here too, teach:
A person – the guarding of his body is upon him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a defense of רב's view from the earlier part of the daf.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה fits רב: a person is responsible to guard himself.

steps.title: רב מרי suggests מבעה means damage by water
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי asks: why not say מבעה means damage done by water? He points to a פסוק that uses the word תבעה (a word from the same root) together with water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי challenges: But say that מבעה is water, as it is written: 'As when fire ignites brushwood, fire boils water.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי offers a new meaning for מבעה: damage caused by water. He bases it on a פסוק where the word תבעה appears next to the word water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words מבעה and תבעה share a root. In the פסוק, תבעה is connected to water, so רב מרי suggests that מבעה might be a category of damage by water. This challenges both רב (person) and שמואל (שן, tooth/eating).

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it; he raised a strong objection
But (why not) say
One of the four main damagers in the משנה; its meaning is being debated
As it is written

phrases.english: Rav Mari challenged it:
But say that 'Maveh' is water,
as it is written: 'As when fire ignites brushwood,'
'fire boils water'!
phrases.notes: The word תבעה shares its root with מבעה. That is the whole basis of the suggestion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new challenge about the meaning of מבעה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanations of מבעה as אדם (רב) or שן (שמואל)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק uses the same root together with water, so maybe מבעה means water damage.

steps.title: Rejected: in the verse, fire is the one doing the boiling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב מרי's idea. The פסוק does not say 'water boils'. It says 'fire boils', so the verb belongs to fire, not water.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it written 'water boiled'? It is written 'fire boils'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב מרי using the grammar of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If water were the one acting, the פסוק would use a plural form like נבעו, since מים is plural. Instead it says תבעה, a singular form that fits אש (fire), which is singular. So the action of the root belongs to fire, and the פסוק gives no proof that מבעה means water.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it written...? (a way of saying: it is not written that way)
They boiled (plural form)
It boils / causes to boil (singular form)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read the פסוק as 'water boils fire'. The words are in an unusual order, but the meaning is 'fire makes water boil'.

phrases.english: Is it written 'water boiled'?!
phrases.notes: מים is a plural word, so if water were doing the action, the verb would be plural like נבעו.

phrases.english: 'Fire boils' is written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב מרי's suggestion from step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully rejects the idea that מבעה means water.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The verb in the פסוק belongs to fire, not to water.

steps.title: רב זביד suggests מבעה means fire
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד builds on the last answer. If the word תבעה in the פסוק belongs to fire, then maybe מבעה means fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד challenges: But say that מבעה is fire, since where 'תבעה' is written, it is written about fire!
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד takes the previous answer and turns it around. He suggests that מבעה means fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 showed that the verb תבעה belongs to fire. רב זביד argues that this same point could prove that מבעה is the category of fire. This sets up a new suggestion that the גמרא will now test against the wording of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Fire
For when it is written

phrases.english: Rav Zevid challenged it:
But say that 'Maveh' is fire,
for when 'tiveh' is written –
it is written about fire!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer from step 3 to make a new suggestion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanations of מבעה as אדם or שן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק links the root to fire, so maybe מבעה is fire.

steps.title: Rejected: the משנה lists מבעה and fire separately
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if מבעה is fire, why does the משנה list both 'מבעה' and 'הבער' (fire) as if they are two different things?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is 'the מבעה and the הבער'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins rejecting רב זביד's idea by pointing to the wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists 'המבעה וההבער', which sounds like two separate categories. הבער is fire, so if מבעה were also fire, the משנה would be naming fire twice.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Burning; the category of fire damage in the משנה

phrases.english: If so, what is 'the Maveh and the Hever'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts rejecting רב זביד's suggestion.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The first argument against מבעה being fire.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה would be listing fire twice.

steps.title: If מבעה only explains fire, there would be just three categories
steps.stepSummary: Someone might answer that 'הבער' just explains what 'מבעה' means. The גמרא replies that then the משנה would have only three categories, but it says four.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say it is explaining, if so, are there four? There are three!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks a possible defense of רב זביד and shows that it breaks the משנה's count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The defense says 'מבעה, that is, הבער' is one item explained, not two items. But the משנה opens with 'four main damagers'. If fire is only one item, the list has only three, so this defense fails.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say
It is just explaining (the previous word)
The four main categories of damage in the משנה

phrases.english: And if you say it is explaining;
phrases.notes: The idea is that 'הבער' would just be telling us what 'מבעה' means.

phrases.english: if so, four?! They are three!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a possible defense against step 5 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It leaves the משנה with three categories instead of four.

steps.title: Fire has no living spirit, but the משנה says מבעה does
steps.stepSummary: Another defense: maybe שור counts as two (רגל and שן), so the total is still four. The גמרא answers that the משנה describes מבעה as having רוח חיים, and fire has no life.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say it teaches 'ox', which includes two; if so, 'not this and that which have a living spirit'. What living spirit does fire have?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks a second defense of רב זביד by pointing to another line of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The defense keeps the count at four by treating שור as two categories, foot and tooth. But the משנה says that שור and מבעה both have רוח חיים. Fire is not alive, so מבעה cannot be fire.

keyTerms.meaning: Which has two (categories) in it
A living spirit; being alive
Not this one and that one (a phrase from the משנה)

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא, תְּנָא שׁוֹר דְּאִית בֵּיהּ תַּרְתֵּי;
phrases.english: And if you say, it taught 'ox', which has two in it;
phrases.notes: The two would be foot (רגל) and tooth (שן). That would bring the count back to four.

phrases.english: if so, 'not this and that'
'which have a living spirit' –
phrases.notes: This is the משנה's description of שור and מבעה together.

phrases.aramaic: אֵשׁ מַאי רוּחַ חַיִּים אִית בֵּיהּ?
phrases.english: what living spirit does fire have?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא, תְּנָא שׁוֹר דְּאִית בֵּיהּ תַּרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a second defense of רב זביד and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the defense that שור counts as two.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה calls מבעה a living thing, and fire is not alive.

steps.title: The משנה compares מבעה to fire, so it cannot be fire
steps.stepSummary: A further proof: the משנה goes on to say these are 'not like fire'. That means מבעה is something different from fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, what is 'like the fire'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a final proof that רב זביד's idea fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that שור and מבעה are not like fire. You cannot compare something to itself. So מבעה must be a separate category, not fire.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore
Like the case of fire (a phrase from the משנה)

steps.whatToRemember: מבעה does not mean water (the פסוק's verb belongs to fire), and it does not mean fire (the משנה lists them separately, counts four, calls מבעה alive, and compares it to fire). So the debate stays between רב (person) and שמואל (tooth).

phrases.english: And furthermore, what is 'like the fire'?
phrases.notes: The משנה says שור and מבעה are 'not like fire'. A thing can't be compared to itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds one more proof against רב זביד.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Finishes rejecting the idea that מבעה is fire.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה compares מבעה to fire, so they must be different things.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: מבעה is neither water nor fire.

steps.title: רבי אושעיא counts thirteen categories of damage
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא teaches that there are thirteen main categories of damage: four kinds of watchmen, five kinds of payment for injury, and the four from our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אושעיא taught: there are thirteen main categories of damage. The unpaid watchman, the borrower, the paid watchman and the renter. Damage, pain, medical costs, lost work and embarrassment. Add the four of our משנה, and that makes thirteen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching of רבי אושעיא that lists thirteen main categories of damage instead of the four in our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says there are four אבות נזיקין. רבי אושעיא adds nine more: four types of watchmen and five types of payment owed for hurting a person. This sets up the obvious question of why our משנה leaves these out.

keyTerms.meaning: An unpaid watchman who looks after someone else's item for free
A borrower
A paid watchman
A renter
The five payments for injuring a person: damage, pain, medical costs, lost work, embarrassment

phrases.english: Rabbi Oshaya taught:
There are thirteen main categories of damage:
the unpaid watchman, and the borrower,
the paid watchman, and the renter;
damage, pain, and medical costs,
lost work, and embarrassment;
and the four of our משנה. That makes thirteen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: a different, longer list of the main categories of damage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are thirteen main categories of damage: 4 watchmen + 5 payments + the 4 of the משנה.

steps.title: Why does our משנה leave out these nine?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why our משנה doesn't list the extra nine. For שמואל, who says the משנה only lists damage done by one's property, this is fine. For רב, who says the משנה includes אדם, it is a problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why doesn't our תנא teach these? According to שמואל it makes sense: the משנה talks about damage done by your property, not damage done by your own body. But according to רב, the משנה should list them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב: if our משנה includes a person who does damage, why doesn't it also list רבי אושעיא's extra categories?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רב said מבעה means a person, and שמואל said it means an animal eating. According to שמואל, all four in the משנה are damage done by your property, so body-related damage is simply not the topic. According to רב, the משנה already talks about a person causing damage, so the extra nine should be included.

keyTerms.meaning: Our תנא, meaning the author of our משנה
It makes sense, it works out fine (used before a 'but' that is a problem)
Damage done by one's property (like an animal or a pit)
Damage done by one's own body

phrases.english: And our תנא, what is the reason
that he does not teach these?
It makes sense according to שמואל:
phrases.notes: שמואל is the one who said מבעה means an animal eating, not a person.

phrases.english: he is talking about damage done by property;
about damage done by one's body he is not talking.
But according to רב, let him teach them!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנָּא דִּידַן מַאי טַעְמָא לָא תָּנֵי הָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי אושעיא's longer list to challenge רב's reading of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that מבעה in the משנה means a person
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the משנה already covers a person causing damage, it should also list the body-related damages that רבי אושעיא counts.

steps.title: The word 'person' already includes everything a person does
steps.stepSummary: According to רב, the משנה taught 'person', and that one word includes all the kinds of damage a person causes.
steps.simpleTranslation: He taught 'person', and that covers everything a person does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב: the משנה did not need to list the extra nine, because 'person' already includes them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The watchmen and the five payments are all cases of a person being responsible. By listing אדם as one category, the משנה covers all of them in one word. So there is no missing information in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: All matters of a person: every kind of damage a person causes

phrases.english: He taught 'person',
and that includes all matters of a person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רב.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Broad reading of one word in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה left out the nine categories, which is a problem for רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The single category 'person' already contains all nine.

steps.title: Then why does רבי אושעיא list them separately?
steps.stepSummary: If 'person' covers everything, רבי אושעיא's list already includes the משנה's 'person'. Why does he also add the nine?
steps.simpleTranslation: And for רבי אושעיא too, he already teaches 'person'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns the answer back on רבי אושעיא: his list already includes 'person', so why count the nine separately?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אושעיא includes 'the four of our משנה', and according to רב one of those four is אדם. If אדם covers all damages a person causes, then adding the watchmen and the five payments would be counting the same thing twice.

keyTerms.meaning: But he already taught it!

phrases.english: And according to רבי אושעיא too,
he already teaches 'person'!
phrases.notes: He means: 'person' is one of the four from the משנה that רבי אושעיא counts in his thirteen.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא נָמֵי הָא תָּנֵי לֵיהּ אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the answer of step 11 and uses it to challenge רבי אושעיא's counting.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'person' already includes all damage done by a person, listing the nine extra items is double counting.

steps.title: Two kinds of 'person'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא splits 'person' into two: a person who hurts a person, and a person who damages an ox (property).
steps.simpleTranslation: There are two kinds of 'person'. He taught a person who hurts a person, and he taught a person who damages an ox.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אושעיא is not double counting, because he is listing two different kinds of damage done by a person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'person' from the משנה is a person who damages property, like someone's ox. The extra items in רבי אושעיא's list are about a person who hurts another person. Since these are two separate types, both get counted.

keyTerms.meaning: Two kinds, two types
Who damages

phrases.english: There are two kinds of 'person':
he taught a person who damages a person,
and he taught a person who damages an ox.
phrases.notes: 'Ox' here stands for anyone's property, not only an actual ox.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge on רבי אושעיא's counting.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting one category into two types
steps.terutzMaskana: He counts two different types: a person hurting a person, and a person damaging property.

steps.title: Then he should count two kinds of ox too
steps.stepSummary: If רבי אושעיא splits 'person' into two, he should also split 'ox' into two: an ox that damages an ox, and an ox that hurts a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, ox too: let him teach two kinds of ox. Let him teach an ox that damages an ox, and let him teach an ox that hurts a person!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last answer: if splitting by victim is the rule, the same should apply to ox. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 13 split 'person' by who gets hurt. By that same logic, 'ox' should also be split into two, which would change the total beyond thirteen. Since רבי אושעיא did not do this, the answer seems inconsistent.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Let him teach (it should have been taught)

phrases.english: If so, ox as well:
let him teach two kinds of ox:
let him teach an ox that damages an ox,
and let him teach an ox that damages a person!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי שׁוֹר נָמֵי לִיתְנֵי תְּרֵי גַוְונֵי שׁוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 13 by applying its own logic to ox.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that רבי אושעיא counts two kinds of 'person'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If damages are split by who is hurt, ox should also be split into two, and רבי אושעיא did not do that.

steps.title: Splitting 'ox' would not change anything
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the challenge from Step 14. 'Person' is split because a person pays different amounts depending on whom he hurts, but an ox's owner pays only for the damage either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: What kind of comparison is this? It makes sense for a person: if he damages an ox, he pays only for the damage, but if he injures a person, he also pays four extra kinds of payment. But for an ox, what difference does it make whether it damages an ox or injures a person? Either way the owner pays only for the damage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of Step 14 by showing that 'ox' and 'person' are not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A category is worth splitting only if the two halves have different laws. When a person injures a person, he pays four extra payments, so 'person who hurts a person' really is a different category. When an ox hurts someone, the owner pays only for the damage, whether the victim was an ox or a person, so there is nothing to split.

keyTerms.meaning: What is this? A phrase used to reject a comparison as not fitting.
Granted, it makes sense that…
Payment for the actual damage done
Four extra payments a person owes when he injures another person
This one and that one, meaning both cases

phrases.english: What is this comparison?
Granted, a person who damages an ox
pays only for the damage;
a person who injures a person
pays four extra things;
but with an ox,
what difference does it make to me, an ox that damages an ox,
or an ox that injures a person?
In both cases, he pays only for the damage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 14 by rejecting its comparison between 'person' and 'ox'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: the split matters only where the law is different.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If 'person' is split in two, 'ox' should be split in two as well.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only 'person' is split, because only a person pays differently depending on the victim. An ox's owner pays plain damage either way.

steps.title: The four watchmen are also a person damaging property
steps.stepSummary: The four kinds of watchmen are cases of a person damaging someone's property, which should already be covered by 'person'. Yet רבי אושעיא lists them separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the unpaid watchman, the borrower, the paid watchman and the renter are all cases of a person damaging property, and still רבי אושעיא lists them as separate categories!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim that 'person' in רבי אושעיא's list already covers a person who damages property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 said רבי אושעיא's 'person' covers a person who damages property. But when a watchman fails to return what he was guarding, that is also a person causing a loss to property. So why does רבי אושעיא count the watchmen separately instead of including them under 'person'?

keyTerms.meaning: An unpaid watchman, who guards something for free
A borrower
A paid watchman
A renter
And yet he teaches it (lists it separately)

phrases.english: But aren't there the unpaid watchman and the borrower,
the paid watchman and the renter,
which are cases of a person who damages an ox,
phrases.notes: 'Ox' here stands for any property, like the item the watchman was supposed to guard.

phrases.english: and yet he lists them!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא שׁוֹמֵר חִנָּם וְהַשּׁוֹאֵל נוֹשֵׂא שָׂכָר וְהַשּׂוֹכֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 15 defends the split of 'person', this step attacks the idea that 'person damaging property' is fully covered by 'person'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation from Step 13 that רבי אושעיא's 'person' already includes a person who damages property.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'person' already covers damaging property, the four watchmen, who are also people causing a loss to property, should not be listed separately. Since he does list them, something does not fit.

steps.title: Direct damage versus damage that happens by itself
steps.stepSummary: 'Person' covers damage someone does with his own hands. The watchmen are listed separately because their damage happens on its own, through lack of guarding.
steps.simpleTranslation: He teaches damage done directly with one's hands, and he also teaches damage that happens on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 16 by showing that 'person' and the watchmen are two different kinds of damage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Person' means someone who actively causes harm. A watchman usually does not do anything. The item gets lost or damaged while it is under his care, so the loss happens by itself. Since these are two different kinds of damage, רבי אושעיא counts them separately.

keyTerms.meaning: Damage done directly, with one's own hands
Damage that happens on its own, without a direct act

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אושעיא splits 'person' only where the law differs (Step 15). He lists the watchmen separately because their damage happens on its own, not through a direct act (Step 17).

phrases.english: He teaches damage done directly with the hands,
and he also teaches damage that happens on its own.
phrases.notes: The second kind means the watchmen, whose loss usually happens through not guarding well, not through an act.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the categories: direct damage versus damage that happens on its own.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The watchmen are just a person damaging property, so listing them is a repeat.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Person' means direct damage. The watchmen are a different type, damage that happens on its own, so they get their own entries.

steps.title: רבי חייא's list of twenty-four main categories begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a new teaching: רבי חייא counts twenty-four main categories of damage, starting with double payment, four- and five-fold payment, a thief, a robber, and plotting witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא teaches: there are twenty-four main categories of damage: double payment, four- and five-fold payment, a thief, a robber, plotting witnesses…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third list of main categories, from רבי חייא, and begins reading it. The list continues in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה lists four categories and רבי אושעיא lists thirteen. Now רבי חייא lists twenty-four, which includes payments from theft and from lying witnesses. The גמרא will go on to explain how these lists relate to each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Twenty-four main categories of damage
Double payment, which a convicted thief pays
Four- or five-fold payment, owed by a thief who slaughters or sells a stolen sheep or ox
A robber, who takes things openly by force
Plotting witnesses who are caught testifying falsely

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up גנב (a thief, who steals secretly) and גזלן (a robber, who takes openly by force). They are two separate entries in the list.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya teaches:
There are twenty-four main categories of damage:
double payment,
and four- and five-fold payment,
and a thief, and a robber, and plotting witnesses,

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא, עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה אֲבוֹת נְזִיקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the discussion of רבי אושעיא's list, the גמרא opens a new list from רבי חייא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חייא counts twenty-four main categories of damage. The list begins with double payment, four- and five-fold payment, a thief, a robber, and plotting witnesses.

steps.title: Finishing the list of twenty-four
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא's list continues with אונס, מפתה, מוציא שם רע, מטמא, מדמע and מנסך. Adding רבי אושעיא's thirteen gives twenty-four.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the rapist, the seducer, the one who spreads a bad name, the one who makes another's תרומה impure, the one who mixes תרומה into another's food, and the one who pours another's wine for idol worship. Add these to the thirteen, and you get twenty-four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting רבי חייא's list from Step 18 and adds up the total.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא's own additions come to eleven: the five from Step 18 and the six here. He also counts the thirteen of רבי אושעיא, so the full list reaches twenty-four.

keyTerms.meaning: one who forces a girl into relations; he pays a fine
one who seduces an unmarried girl; he pays a fine
a husband who falsely claims his wife was unfaithful; he pays a fine
one who makes another person's תרומה impure
one who mixes תרומה into another person's regular food
one who pours another person's wine as an offering to idols

phrases.english: and the rapist, and the seducer,
and one who spreads a bad name,
phrases.notes: This is a husband who falsely says in court that his new wife was unfaithful.

phrases.english: and one who makes impure, and one who mixes, and one who pours as a libation;
phrases.notes: All three ruin someone else's food or wine: impure תרומה, תרומה mixed into regular food, or wine poured for idols.

phrases.english: and these thirteen —
that makes twenty-four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quotation of רבי חייא begun in Step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חייא's eleven extra categories plus רבי אושעיא's thirteen make twenty-four main categories of damage.

steps.title: Why does רבי אושעיא leave these out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אושעיא does not include רבי חייא's extra eleven categories.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אושעיא: why doesn't he teach these?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי אושעיא's list is missing the items that רבי חייא includes. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both lists are meant to count the main categories of damage. If רבי חייא's extra items really are damages, the גמרא wants to know what reason רבי אושעיא had for leaving them out.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the reason?
he does not teach (does not list)

phrases.english: And רבי אושעיא —
what is the reason he does not teach these?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא – מַאי טַעְמָא לָא תָּנֵי הָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares רבי חייא's longer list with רבי אושעיא's shorter one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason רבי אושעיא omits רבי חייא's extra categories.

steps.title: רבי אושעיא only lists money repayment, not fines
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא lists only cases of paying back actual money, not fines.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is talking about paying money back. He is not talking about fines.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אושעיא's list only includes cases where a person pays back the actual loss, so he leaves out fines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קנס is a set penalty, like double payment or the fifty סלע of the אונס. It is not simply paying back the loss. רבי חייא counts these, but רבי אושעיא's list is limited to ממון.

keyTerms.meaning: money (paying back the actual loss)
a fine (a set penalty, not just the loss)
he is talking about

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the fines are not real obligations. They are fully binding. רבי אושעיא just chose to count only one kind of payment.

phrases.english: He speaks about money repayment;
he does not speak about fines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אושעיא's list covers only ממון (repayment of loss), not קנס (fines).

steps.title: But a thief and a robber pay money
steps.stepSummary: גנב and גזלן pay back money, not a fine, so רבי אושעיא should have listed them.
steps.simpleTranslation: A thief and a robber pay back money. He should list them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 21. Two items on רבי חייא's list are cases of ממון, so the fines answer does not explain why they are missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Returning stolen property is plain repayment, not a fine. So the reason from Step 21 cannot explain why רבי אושעיא leaves out גנב and גזלן.

keyTerms.meaning: a thief (takes in secret)
a robber (takes openly, by force)
let him teach it (he should list it)

phrases.english: A thief and a robber,
which is money, let him teach them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי אושעיא omits only fines.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: גנב and גזלן are cases of ממון, yet they are missing from רבי אושעיא's list.

steps.title: He already covers them with שומר חנם and שואל
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא does include these cases, through the שומר חנם and the שואל on his list.
steps.simpleTranslation: He does teach them: he lists the unpaid watchman and the borrower.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אושעיא does cover theft. The cases of the watchmen on his list already include it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שומר חנם who falsely claims the item he was guarding was stolen pays like a thief. So listing the watchmen already covers the law of stealing money, and a separate גנב and גזלן are not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: an unpaid watchman
a borrower
but he does teach it!

phrases.english: But he does teach it:
the unpaid watchman and the borrower.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא קָתָנֵי לֵיהּ שׁוֹמֵר חִנָּם וְהַשּׁוֹאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the case is already included in another listed category.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אושעיא's list leaves out theft entirely.
steps.terutzMaskana: Theft of money is covered by שומר חנם and שואל on his list.

steps.title: Then why does רבי חייא list both?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא also lists שומר חנם and שואל, so why does he add גנב and גזלן separately?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חייא too lists the unpaid watchman and the borrower! So why list thief and robber as well?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answer from Step 23 against רבי חייא. If the watchmen cover theft, his separate listing of גנב and גזלן looks like it says the same thing twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 said that שומר חנם and שואל already include theft. But רבי חייא lists both the watchmen and the thieves, which seems to count the same thing two times.

keyTerms.meaning: also, too
but he already taught it!

phrases.english: And רבי חייא too,
he already taught it:
the unpaid watchman and the borrower!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא נָמֵי, הָא תְּנָא לֵיהּ שׁוֹמֵר חִנָּם וְהַשּׁוֹאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of Step 23 to question רבי חייא's list.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא's listing of גנב and גזלן next to שומר חנם and שואל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the watchmen already cover theft, listing thief and robber as well repeats the same thing.

steps.title: Permitted possession versus forbidden possession
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא lists both because the watchmen got the money in a permitted way, while the thief and robber took it in a forbidden way.
steps.simpleTranslation: He teaches money that came into his hands in a permitted way, and he also teaches money that came into his hands in a forbidden way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי חייא is counting two different kinds of cases, so listing both is not a repeat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A watchman or borrower received the item legally and only later kept it dishonestly. A גנב or גזלן took it wrongly from the start. רבי חייא counts these as two separate kinds, while רבי אושעיא lets the watchmen stand for both.

keyTerms.meaning: in a permitted way
in a forbidden way
that came into his hands

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אושעיא's list counts only ממון, not קנס. Theft is covered on his list by the watchmen. רבי חייא lists theft separately because he divides money held in a permitted way (watchmen) from money taken in a forbidden way (גנב, גזלן).

phrases.english: He teaches money
that came into his hands in a permitted way,
and he also teaches money
that came into his hands in a forbidden way.
phrases.notes: This means the thief and the robber.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Draws a distinction between two kinds of possession.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Listing thief and robber next to the watchmen repeats the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Money received in a permitted way and money taken in a forbidden way are counted as separate categories.
